note: boots: the arm at the platform default, the same binary with revocation off, and (when --eager) a third at every-free. The default is the only one a verdict comes from; off is what attributes a fault, since a purecap SIGPROT carries no symbol here; eager only separates a quarantined-but-never-reissued chunk from a genuine miss, and is recorded in the notes rather than scored

platform.compiler: the CheriBSD SDK clang that built ports/php/cheribsd

boot_provenance.boots_read: the three cheribsd-*.json records under the raw run directory for 2026-10-29
boot_provenance.eager_boot_rerun: The eager boot was run twice. THE FIRST IS VOID AND IS NOT THE ONE READ HERE: a concurrent run of the same driver rewrote the guest script in the shared stage directory while it was executing, and its transcript ends after 9 of 31 entries with a garbled console. The driver now names the guest script after its own pid so two runs cannot collide. The boot read here is the re-run, which also carries the auto_append_file END marker that places each eager fault inside the script body or in request shutdown.
boot_provenance.placement_control: A boot where no case printed PHPB_TRIGGER_END cannot place a fault, and the runner now says `unplaced` instead of defaulting to `inside the script body`. Both corpora's eager boots were re-run with the marker for that reason.
